62.points: Rabby runs Rabby Points for using the wallet.

63.points: MetaMask Rewards, in the mobile app, gives points for trading challenges and can include airdrops and partner perks.

68.yield: The HLP vault earns from market making and liquidations, so returns swing with trader profit and loss: about 3.7% average over the last 30 days. USDC lending earns about 3% to 4%.
68.points: Hyperliquid's HYPE airdrop to points holders happened in November 2024.
68.note: HLP can lose money when traders win big against it.

87.yield: Lending rates float with demand. Stablecoin supply rates run up to about 5.6% APY on the bigger markets; ETH earns around 1.4%.

90.yield: Staking USDe as sUSDe earns about 5.0% APY (30-day average 5.0%). Yield comes from funding rates, so it can drop sharply in bear markets.
90.points: Runs the Sats campaign: holding or staking USDe and locking ENA earns Sats, which convert to ENA at the end of each season. Season 6 was reported live from March 26, 2026.
90.note: Unstaking sUSDe has a 7-day cooldown before you get USDe back.

102.yield: Staking SOL as JitoSOL earns about 4.8% APY, including MEV rewards.

104.yield: Fixed yields on stablecoin markets mostly run about 5% to 10% APY, with some higher. You lock the rate until the market's maturity date.
104.note: Selling a fixed-rate position before maturity happens at the market price, which can be lower than what you paid.

105.yield: Stablecoin lending runs up to about 7% APY (PYUSD around 6.9%, part of it paid in reward tokens).
105.points: Kamino moved from points to direct KMNO rewards paid on lending and liquidity activity.

106.yield: Pool yields vary: big stablecoin pools earn little in fees, while some crvUSD and DOLA pools pay roughly 2% to 7.5%, often partly in CRV rewards. LPs also carry pool and depeg risk.

108.yield: Pool yields range from under 1% to around 8% APY, depending on the pool and its incentives.

110.yield: Yields come from trading fees on each liquidity pool and swing a lot with volume. Volatile pairs can show very high APRs along with impermanent loss risk.

119.yield: Restaking ETH as weETH earns about 2.5% to 2.9% APY; the Liquid ETH vault about 3.5% to 3.9%; the Liquid USD vault about 5.3%.
119.points: ether.fi has ended its traditional seasonal points program. Check the app for any current campaigns.

125.yield: Curated stablecoin vaults mostly earn about 5% to 7% APY; for example, Steakhouse USDC on Base is around 5%.

132.yield: Supply rates float with demand. Stablecoin markets earn up to about 7.6% APY; ETH and BTC markets earn little.

152.points: Lighter's LIT token launched in December 2025, with 25% of supply airdropped to Season 1 and 2 points holders. A new points season had not been announced as of mid-2026.

155.yield: Liquidity providers earn trading fees. Major WETH/USDC pools recently showed roughly 25% to 45% APR from fees; stable pairs under 1%. Impermanent loss can outweigh fees.

165.points: Runs xPoints (since March 2026) for trading, holding and providing liquidity with xStocks, for non-US users. No token has been confirmed.

171.yield: LP rewards are paid mostly in AERO and vary widely: stable pairs earn low single digits, while volatile pairs can show triple-digit APRs that move fast.

174.yield: Jupiter Lend pays about 4.8% APY on USDC (30-day average 6.3%). Staking SOL as JupSOL earns about 5.1%.

180.yield: Staking SOL as bpSOL earns about 5.4% to 5.6% APY. Backpack also pays interest on some exchange balances.
180.points: Backpack's points seasons ended with its BP token launch and airdrop in March 2026.

181.yield: Vault yields range widely: stablecoin vaults about 5% to 13% APY, depending on the vault and its strategy risk.

185.yield: Staking SOL as bulkSOL earned about 4.6% APY on average over the last 30 days.
185.points: Runs AURA points for pre-deposits, trading, staking and referrals ahead of an expected airdrop. No token date or conversion rate has been published.

197.yield: Solana yield markets let you lock a fixed rate or trade variable yield. Rates depend on the market and its maturity date; check each market's implied APY.
197.points: Has a Points Hub that tracks your Exponent points, and many markets pass through partner points (for example Hylo XP or Solstice Flares). No Exponent token has been confirmed.

200.yield: ONyc, its reinsurance-backed yield token, earns about 11% APY.
200.note: ONyc is backed by reinsurance, so returns depend on insurance claims as well as markets.

203.yield: Staking SOL as hyloSOL earns about 5.4% APY. Its stablecoin and leveraged tokens carry their own yields and risks.
203.points: Runs an XP program: holding Hylo products like xSOL and hyUSD earns XP. No token or airdrop has been confirmed.

204.points: Runs Flares points, which are set to convert into SLX tokens. Using USX and eUSX, including on partner apps, earns Flares.

205.points: Runs Omni points (since December 2025), earned from trading volume. A VAR token with a large community airdrop is expected, but no launch date has been confirmed.

206.yield: USDC lending earns about 6% to 7.5% APY; some markets add reward tokens on top.
206.points: Deposits earn Loopscale points, more when actively lent out, plus a share of points from people you refer. No token or airdrop date has been announced.

320.yield: Staking trUSD as strUSD earns about 10% APY (30-day average 9.9%). Returns come from market-neutral trading strategies and can change.
320.points: Runs Cores points (Season 1 started June 2026): holding trUSD or strUSD and using them in partner apps like Morpho, Pendle and Curve earns Cores. No token has been confirmed.
320.note: Unstaking strUSD has a 7-day cooldown before you can swap back to USDC or USDT.
